findings.title: Authorize team admins or owners, not both roles at once
findings.body: The team authorization check combines isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with &&. A team member with either the ADMIN or OWNER role should be allowed, but requiring both excludes admins/owners who are not also the booking organizer or an attendee. Use an OR check so team administrators can add guests to their team's bookings.

findings.title: Update the calendar using the booking organizer's credentials
findings.body: This handler allows attendees and team administrators to add guests, but constructs EventManager with the calling user's credentials rather than the booking organizer's. When an attendee adds a guest, those credentials cannot update the organizer's calendar event (and may contain no calendar integration at all). The database has already been updated at this point, leaving the attendee list out of sync with the actual calendar invitation. Load and use the booking owner's credentials for this update.

findings.title: Deduplicate the submitted guest list on the server
findings.body: uniqueGuests only removes addresses already present in the booking; it does not remove duplicates within guests. The server schema accepts repeated addresses, so a direct mutation with the same new email twice passes this filter and sends both entries to createMany, producing duplicate attendees or a database constraint failure. The dialog's uniqueness validation does not protect the API. Deduplicate or reject duplicate addresses server-side before writing.

findings.title: Normalize guest emails before checking the blacklist
findings.body: BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS is lowercased when loaded, but the submitted guest address is compared without lowercasing it. A blacklisted address submitted with an uppercase character passes validation and is added and emailed. Normalize the submitted address before comparing it to the blacklist so casing cannot bypass this restriction.

findings.title: Respect disabled standard-email settings for guest notifications
findings.body: sendAddGuestsEmails unconditionally emails the organizer and every attendee and does not accept event-type metadata. Other booking notification functions in this file honor disableStandardEmails.all.host and disableStandardEmails.all.attendee. Adding a guest therefore sends standard booking emails even for event types configured to suppress them, potentially duplicating custom workflow notifications. Pass the event-type metadata from the handler and apply the existing host/attendee suppression checks.
